messages:
Ava: Quick sketch — thinking about a graceful cutover for sparse-enqueue patterns. Idea: add a short 'grace window' where queues accept sparse requests and we do predictive-fill to avoid starving the batcher.
Ravi: How long are you thinking for the window? 50-200ms?
Ava: Start with 120ms, tunable per-model. We saw tail latency spikes when we clipped earlier.
Jules: Curious about fairness — won't predictive-fill favor noisy tenants and worsen starvation for low-qps tenants?
Priya: We can cap per-tenant fill budget and track usage. Also use eviction hysteresis so we don't thrash low-qps tenants out repeatedly.
Ava: Plan: per-tenant soft-cap, window-based predictive fill, then after the grace window a hard cutover to coalesce-only fastpath. Grace window gives short headroom for low-rate bursts without hurting long-lived throughput.
Ravi: What about KV cache pressure when we fill gaps? Extra prefixes could bloat the cache and evict useful entries.
Priya: Mark predictive entries ephemeral with short TTL and exclude them from long-term eviction score. Also limit predictive keys per host.
Jules: Telemetry needs: fill_hit_rate, added_tokens, latency_delta_per-tenant, cache_churn, eviction_retries. Without those we won't know if fairness regresses.
infra-bot: test-deploy queued: canary north-1 tonight, feature toggle `enable_sparse_grace` will be set to true for control group.
Ava: I'll draft an experiment RFC with knobs: window_ms, per_tenant_fill_budget, ephemeral_ttl_ms, cpu_backoff_threshold.
Ravi: Add a CPU fallback: if host CPU > 70% disable predictive-fill to avoid overload.
Priya: Also add a canary harness that synthesizes low-qps tenants interleaved with high-qps ones so we can validate fairness percentiles.
Jules: Edge case: what if a tenant spikes repeatedly at t+window? Need hysteresis so we don't keep granting grace over and over. Maybe exponential backoff on subsequent windows.
Ava: Good call. We'll track last_grace_ts per-tenant and backoff multiplier.
Ravi: Implementation owners? Ava + Ravi take runtime bits, Priya owns telemetry and dashboard slices, Jules will own the fairness test harness.
Ava: I'll open the PR and include a short runnable throughput test and config defaults. Will link the canary once deploys finish.
Priya: Ping me with the telemetry schema so I can add dashboards/alerts.
Jules: SGTM. If the canary looks stable we'll roll to dedicated pools next week.
Ava: Thanks — will follow up in the RFC thread and include sample graphs.
